sections.title: The Concept: From ODEs to PDEs
sections.content: Briefly recap Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) which involve one independent variable (like time). Introduce PDEs as the mathematical language for systems varying in multiple dimensions (e.g., space and time simultaneously). Use a visual transition showing a single path (ODE) expanding into a complex surface (PDE).
sections.example: Comparing a 1D timeline of a single runner (ODE) to a 2D weather map showing wind pressure across a city (PDE).

sections.title: Visualizing the Heat Equation
sections.content: Explain the Heat Equation: a classic PDE describing how temperature diffuses over time and space. Use an animated 3D surface plot where the 'height' represents temperature, showing it smoothing out over time as the gradient flattens.
sections.example: A curious cat sitting on a heated metal plate; show the heat spreading from the center to the edges as time progresses.

sections.title: The Wave Equation: Vibrations in Motion
sections.content: Introduce the Wave Equation. Explain that while heat dissipates, waves oscillate. Use a sine-wave animation on a string. Highlight that the 'second derivative' in space and time captures the curvature (tension) of the wave.
sections.example: A guitar string plucked by a musician; visualize the vertical movement of the string as a function of its position (x) and time (t).

sections.title: Boundary Conditions: The 'Rules' of the System
sections.content: Explain that a PDE is unsolvable without boundary conditions. Use a box animation: if the 'edges' of the box are held at 0 degrees, the internal temperature distribution is constrained by those fixed walls.
sections.example: A goldfish in a tank; the water flow (PDE) is constrained by the shape and material of the glass walls (Boundary Conditions).

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Impact
sections.content: Conclude by emphasizing that PDEs are the backbone of modern science. Briefly mention their role in aerodynamics, finance (Black-Scholes), and medical imaging.
sections.example: A high-speed animation showing how engineers use PDEs to design the sleek, aerodynamic shape of a futuristic drone.

PDEs describe systems changing in multiple dimensions.
Visualize an ODE path expanding into a PDE surface.

storyboard.title: The Wave Equation: Vibrations in Motion
lecture_lines: The Wave Equation models oscillations on a string.
It captures how waves move through space and time.
Visualize a sine-wave string vibrating continuously.

storyboard.title: Boundary Conditions: The 'Rules' of the System
lecture_lines: PDEs require boundary conditions to find unique solutions.
Boundary conditions act like rules for the system.
Visualize fixed edges constraining the internal state.

Animate a wave reflecting off the fixed boundaries.
Add a text label 'Constraint' near the boundary.

lecture_lines: PDEs are fundamental to modern science and engineering.
They model aerodynamics, finance, and medical imaging.
They enable advanced technology and scientific discovery.
